subsystems.name: Electrode array
subsystems.role: picks up the tiny voltages that motor nerves trigger in forearm muscles; typically 8–64 dry electrodes around the wrist.

subsystems.name: Analog front end
subsystems.role: amplifies microvolt-level signals before they are digitised, without drowning them in mains hum.
parts: analog-to-digital converter sampling at 1–2 kHz or more

subsystems.name: Motion and context sensing
subsystems.role: separates intended gestures from arm movement and changing skin contact.

subsystems.name: On-device decoding
subsystems.role: turns raw waveforms into finger positions or discrete commands.

subsystems.name: Wireless link and power
subsystems.role: sends commands to a phone, headset or computer and runs all day.

subsystems.name: Calibration and training pipeline
subsystems.role: personalises the decoder, since every forearm's signal pattern differs.
parts: paired ground-truth capture (cameras or sensor gloves)

buildSteps.title: Map the signal source
buildSteps.detail: Researchers measure where hand and finger motor-unit activity appears around the wrist to choose electrode positions. This is muscle electrical activity driven by motor neurons, not raw nerve impulses — true nerve signals need implanted electrodes.

buildSteps.title: Design the band
buildSteps.detail: Electrodes are arranged in a ring so that contact stays stable as the wrist flexes, with dry materials that work without gel.

buildSteps.title: Build the front end
buildSteps.detail: Instrumentation amplifiers with high common-mode rejection and tight band-pass filtering are laid out to keep noise below the few-microvolt signals of interest.

buildSteps.title: Write firmware
buildSteps.detail: The device samples continuously, tracks electrode contact quality, and streams windows of data over a low-power radio.

buildSteps.title: Collect labelled data
buildSteps.detail: A wearer performs prompted gestures and finger movements while cameras or gloves record the ground truth, building a paired dataset.

buildSteps.title: Train the decoder
buildSteps.detail: A neural network learns to map signal windows to intended hand poses or commands, then is compressed to run on the band itself.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate per user
buildSteps.detail: A short guided routine adapts the model to the wearer's anatomy, sweat and session; much research targets making this step unnecessary.

buildSteps.title: Validate in daily use
buildSteps.detail: Testing across sessions, arm positions, temperature and sweat shows how often the decoder is wrong — the main barrier to shipping.

prerequisites.why: decades of ECG and EMG hardware already deliver amplifiers and electrodes sensitive enough for the wrist.
research prototypes decode hand intent, but accuracy often degrades between sessions and users.
most systems need user-specific training data; a consumer product needs it to work out of the box.
phones and earbuds have driven down the size and power needed to run a small model all day.
without a way to send touch back to the user, commands are one-way only.

pathway.milestone: research wristbands decoding simple gestures and finger movements with per-user calibration
pathway.unlocks: hands-free control of glasses, phones and computers in lab and demo settings.

pathway.milestone: continuous finger-level tracking that holds up across sessions, sweat and arm posture
pathway.unlocks: typing-free text entry and precise cursor control without cameras.

pathway.milestone: integrated bands built into consumer wearables and AR glasses
pathway.unlocks: mass-market input that works where keyboards and touchscreens cannot.

pathway.milestone: medical and accessibility use, such as intuitive prosthetic and assistive control
pathway.unlocks: restored function for people with limb loss or motor impairment.

pathway.milestone: bidirectional bands combining sensing with non-invasive stimulation, or fusion with wrist ultrasound imaging
pathway.unlocks: higher-bandwidth, two-way neural interfaces without surgery.
